title: Prepare heavy initialization for lazy loading (first phase)
summary: Names what an initialization section does; --apply moves its body verbatim into a run-once routine, through a scratch build and the compile gate
intro: Read this when the heavy-initialization rule reports a unit and you want the work out of the section. This first phase changes no behaviour: the plan shows which statement is heavy and which global could go lazy, and --apply only extracts the body, so that moving the call later is a one-line change.

help: drag-lint lint <file> --rule debug-display-placeholder --db <db> (default OFF in 1.52; a [DebuggerDisplay('..{Name}..')] placeholder naming no member of the type, read from the attributes index fact; category bug-patterns, warning)

drag-lint lint --in <F> [--db <db>] --enable <rule> --fix --fix-rule <rule> --fix-line <n> [--col <c>] [--name <ident>] [--apply] [--project <X.dproj>] - extract the literal at line n (column c) into a named constant and replace every occurrence in the unit; <rule> = extract-constant (any number or string literal, OFF by default, reports only when its fix is asked for), magic-literal, large-magic-number or case-magic-numbers; risky, manual only (a batch --fix withholds it); report on stderr

drag-lint lint <file.pas> [--rule index-possibly-out-of-range] [--fix --fix-rule index-possibly-out-of-range [--apply]] (default ON, category bug-patterns, warning; hint on an unguarded parameter or a lookup-derived index; param exception_class; the autofix is manual only: a batch --fix withholds it, --fix-rule applies it; rules --json carries fix_manual_only: true)

drag-lint lint <file.pas> [--config <lint.json>] [--no-budget] (lint config key rule_time_budget_ms, default 2000 ms per rule per file, 0 = off; --no-budget or DRAGLINT_NO_BUDGET=1 = off; an overrunning rule is skipped for the file with one rule-skipped-budget note: category other, info, on)
^ A second --db is the library slot, not another project: to judge a dl:ok on a dl:shared unit use --shared-db.

^ `--library-db <lib>` names the library slot too and wins over a second --db and the manifest; a missing file refuses (exit 2), `none` means no library. Without a library, a type whose ancestry lives there stays unknown and the type-aware rules stay silent on it.
^ lint `<file>` is a strict SUBSET: project-wide rules can only fire in lint-all.
^ A vendored folder INSIDE the project folder is linted as your own code until `excludeRoots` names it in `<project>\_D-RAG\drag-lint-project.json`.
drag-lint lint-all --rule member-could-be-private --db <db> (default OFF in 1.52; naming it with --rule runs it, category project-wide, hint)

drag-lint lint-all --db <db> [--rule missing-doc|doc-placeholder|doc-malformed-summary] (documentation rules: missing-doc OFF by default, document all real code, an empty DFM-bound handler is exempt; doc-placeholder ON hint; doc-malformed-summary OFF hint)
drag-lint lint-all --db <file.sqlite> [--no-budget] (same budget; one "rule budget:" note line lists the skipped rules of the run)

drag-lint lint-all --db <file.sqlite> [--project <file.dproj>] [--rule unit-used-by-no-unit|unit-not-in-dpr] (unit-used-by-no-unit: default ON, category project-wide, warning, lint-all only; exempt: initialization section or container registration, a form only when the program code or a FindClass('TName') string opens it; unit-not-in-dpr: the whole compile closure minus the library / third-party roots (registry library paths + manifest Library include), units outside the project roots reported on the .dpr)
